name: Lolo, Pei-shan dialect
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Fu Maoji. 1997 [1950]. A descriptive grammar of Lolo. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 20(1): 1-242 (Cambridge University PhD dissertation, August 1950; Pei-shan dialect, Hsi-ch'ang [Xichang] district, then Sikang, now Liangshan, Sichuan).
catalog_locator: Grammar, II. Phonetics, (4) Stress, §71, pp. 63-64 (LTBA pagination)
catalog_quote: 71. Syllables of a simple or compound word are evenly stressed no matter whether they are affixes or stem words. Thus, in ²a ²ʂo 'long', the prefix ²a has the same stress as the stem word ²ʂo; in the compound ²ia ²ka ¹pi ²du 'pipe-cleaner', the constituent words ²ia ²ka and ¹pi have the same stress as the particle ²du. The words in a phrase, clause, or sentence generally have even stress except in the following cases: (a) A numerative is unstressed when immediately following a substantive or an adjective, as ²ma in the following examples: ²no ²ma 'a Black Lolo' ³mbo ²ma 'a good one' (b) When the speaker wants to emphasize one or more words, these words usually bear stronger stress. ... the word ¹ndu can be emphasized by pronouncing it with a stress stronger than that of all the other words in the sentence. The strongly stressed and the unstressed syllable may retain their ordinary tones, but it often happens that the strongly stressed syllable is especially highly pitched and the unstressed syllable has a pitch lower than its ordinary tone. Stress, however, unlike the tone, is not used to differentiate the meaning of disyllabic words.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tone language (three tones: high level, mid level, low falling). No word-level stress: all syllables of a simple or compound word carry equal stress, prefixes and stems alike; stress is never distinctive. Departures from even stress are phrasal/pragmatic only: a numerative (classifier) directly after a noun or adjective is unstressed, and an emphasized word gets stronger stress, which raises its pitch (unstressed syllables are pitched lower than their ordinary tone).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (no stress hierarchy within the word at all).
new_statements.exceptions: Phrase level only: (a) numeratives unstressed after a substantive/adjective (²no ²ma 'a Black Lolo', ³mbo ²ma 'a good one'); (b) emphatic stress on any word the speaker wishes to highlight (example sentence 'If you do not obey me, I shall beat you' with ¹ndu 'beat' stressed).
new_statements.domain_note: Word (simple and compound) and phrase/clause/sentence both treated; data are 1938-1950 field recordings of the Pei-shan dialect, Hsi-ch'ang (Xichang) district, then Sikang, now Liangshan, Sichuan.
new_statements.identity_note: Fu Maoji's grammar describes the 'Pei-shan' (Beishan) dialect of 'Lolo' in the Hsi-ch'ang (Xichang) district of former Sikang province, now Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan — i.e. Northern Yi / Nuosu (sich1238), in the area of the Shengzha (Shynra) dialect on which standard Nuosu is based; data collected 1938-1950. The other opened sources are the standard Shypnra/Shengza dialect (Edmondson, Esling & Ziwo 2017) and Adur Niesu (Ding 2023), a Nuosu-proper variety Ding says has low mutual intelligibility with Nuosu; neither says anything about stress.

tone_statements.citation: Yang, Renqin. 2020. Analysis and Research on the Tone of Yi Nuo Dialect and Sheng Zha Dialect of Liangshan Nationality. Open Access Library Journal 7: e6701, 7 pp. doi:10.4236/oalib.1106701
tone_statements.quote: The tone of Yi language is 55 (high flat tone), 44 (secondary high tone), 33 (middle flat tone) and 21 (low flat tone). There are three tones in the “Yi Nuo” native language area, which are 35 (high rising tone), 33 (middle flat tone), and 31 (middle falling tone, 42 high falling tone), without any minor tone (Ma jing. 2013) [3]. [...] In Yinuo, the key of 33 is slightly lower, close to 22. When 33 is connected with 33, the first syllable is slightly lower. When the syllables are connected, there will be a variation of 31, which must satisfy the condition of 33 + 35 → 31 + 35. There are three tones in Yinuo dialect and four tones in Shengzha Dialect.
tone_statements.locator: p. 3, section 2 'The Elaboration of the Concept of Tone'

tone_statements.citation: Sha-ma Dage [沙马打各] & Xiao Xue [肖雪]. 2008. On Grammar Functions of Tone Modification in Liangshan Yi Language. Macrolinguistics 2 (Serial No. 2): 127-133. doi:10.26478/ja2008.2.2.7
tone_statements.quote: In the Yi language, tone normally functions to distinguish the meanings of words; that is, tone is lexical. … When a monosyllabic verb in Yi language converts its tone from low-falling tone to sub-high tone, its grammatical relationship with its associated pronoun in a sentence changes from SV to OV. … If a personal pronoun displays mid-level tone, the sentence will be SV. In contrast, if the personal pronoun acquires sub-high tone, the sentence will be OV. When verbs with high-level tone are linked with personal pronouns, neither verb nor personal pronoun may change their tones.
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone; four tones named but never counted: high-level (55), sub-high (34), mid-level (33), low-falling (21). Verb 21->34 and singular pronoun 33->34 mark OV vs SV. Nothing on word stress.

tone_statements.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A., John H. Esling & Lama Ziwo. 2017. Nuosu Yi. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 47(1): 87-97. doi:10.1017/S0025100315000444 (first published online 18 March 2016)
tone_statements.quote: There are three lexical tones in Nuosu Yi, 55 (high level), 33 (mid level), and 21 (low falling), whose pitch is basically the same in either register (lax or tense). There is a 44 (high mid level) tone sandhi realization, which often results from either tone 33 or tone 21 in syllable combination, for example, dza33 'food' + dzɯ33 'to eat' → dza44 dzɯ33 'to eat (food)', and ndʐa33 'to examine' + hɯ21 'to see' → ndʐa33 hɯ44 'to test'. [...] In the case of emphasis, a classifier tone can be read as tone [44], for example, ma44, where tone [44] is originally tone /33/.
